title: Advanced Professional Certificate in Operations and Information Management for Project Managers
description: This course covers the principles and practices of operations and information management essential for project managers to ensure successful project delivery.
longDescription: This course on Operations and Information Management for Project Managers covers a range of topics essential for effective project delivery. It begins with an overview of the role of operations in business management, followed by an exploration of strategic capacity planning and effective inventory management. The course also covers the concept of scheduling in supply chain operations and the importance of project quality management systems. Students will learn about key functions of operations management, production operations and service operations, as well as business process management and reengineering. Additionally, they will gain an understanding of Six Sigma principles for operations improvement, determinants of effective capacity, and bottleneck theory. The course also covers ABC analysis and the economic order quantity model for inventory management, along with approaches to scheduling and load work centers, sequencing, and minimizing scheduling difficulties. Finally, students will learn about quality circles, ISO nine thousand series, and total quality management, including the concept of Kaizen or continuous improvement.

Determinants of Effective Capacity, Capacity Constraints, and Bottleneck Theory study. Inventory Management System, its type, importance, commonly used inventories, effective inventory management, and the component of the Inventory Model. ABC Analysis, the Category of ABC Analysis, Why it is Critical to Use ABC Analysis for Inventory Management, How to Conduct an ABC Analysis, Major Applications of ABC Analysis, and Future Trends in ABC Analysis. Economic Order Quantity Model, Assumptions of EOQ, how to use EOQ in your business, Single Period Model, and Types of Single Period Model. Operation Scheduling, its Objectives, functions, and types. Approaches to scheduling and Load Work Centres, along with concept and method of sequencing, performance measures, and minimizing scheduling difficulties. Theory of Constraints including principles, metrics used, Scheduling Services, Scheduling Multiple Resources, and Time–Cost Trade-Offs. Project Quality Management, its three Processes, Quality Management System's importance, Establishing and Implementing a QMS, and its elements. Total Quality Management, its Principles, Methods, and Steps, along with understanding the Kaizen or Continuous Improvement concept, its types, and Cycle.
